audit.whatIsWrong: The chart said Skill at Level 1, Skill at Level 3, Quinn at Levels 4-5 and Quinn at 2+ items, while the packet chart and the page's own whys say Quinn owns Level 1, Sett owns Level 3 and Levels 4-5, and 2+ items is even.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is [Quinn, Skill, Sett, Sett, Skill, Sett, Skill]. whys[0] 'You own level 1', whys[2] 'out-damages your squishy frame', whys[3] 'wins levels 4-5 outright' and whys[6] 'you stay even only by kiting' all contradicted the rendered sides.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group; rows 1, 4 and 5 left as-is (row 5 stays Quinn because whys[5] and spikes[3] both put the first-item spike on Quinn).

audit.why: Spikes are already correct and unusually specific: Quinn level 1, Sett at W-charged plus E, Sett level 6 with The Show Stopper, Quinn at first lethality item. Real cooldowns now added to the supporting fields.
audit.corrected: Haymaker 18s, Knuckle Down 9s, Facebreaker 16s at rank 1 stated in breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's central instruction — 'blind his W', 'Blind it' against Haymaker — is wrong. Haymaker is a cast ability; a blind only stops basic attacks. It is Knuckle Down (Q) whose empowered punches the blind actually denies. Also missing: The Show Stopper (R) grounds, which denies Vault, and both Facebreaker (E) and The Show Stopper cancel Behind Enemy Lines.
audit.why: Riot text for Haymaker: 'Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area' — an ability cast. Knuckle Down: 'Sett's next two attacks deal additional damage', i.e. basic attacks. The Show Stopper carries the grounding flag; Quinn's R carries the channel flag; the missing-interactions file flags both dash-denied and your-channel-punished for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Blind re-scoped to Knuckle Down, Haymaker reframed as a Grit meter the player fills by poking, and the grounding and channel-cancel interactions stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Haymaker was named the punishable cooldown; the more useful window is Facebreaker (16s at rank 1), since without the grab the smash rarely lands on you.
audit.why: Haymaker has 25000 range in the data and needs no setup; Facebreaker at 490 range is what pins you for it.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker named as the punish window alongside the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker only STUNS when it catches enemies on opposite sides of Sett; a lone target is slowed instead.
audit.why: Riot text: 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' In a 1v1 lane you are usually the only target, so his grab is often a slow, not a stun — that changes whether you can Vault out of it.
audit.corrected: Recorded here; the prose already tells the player to dodge the grab, so no space was spent restating a conditional they cannot control alone.

edits.before: Passive-mark AA trades win every short exchange. Identify how Sett contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: A Harrier-marked auto plus your range wins the first exchange before Pit Grit's double-punch can reach you. Step up and trade.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Sett must walk into your range.
edits.after: His Haymaker is charged and Facebreaker is up — a landed grab feeds the true-damage smash. Poke, do not stand and trade.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Haymaker's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Grit sustain and the stored smash win any stand-still brawl here — take Q pokes and Vault out, and never fight in Facebreaker range.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Sett carry threat 6/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: He stacks HP so his max-health smash scales; you stay even by kiting. Sett carry threat 6/10 — refuse the grab.

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — Shield + true damage. Blind it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Haymaker (W): 18s at rank 1, shield plus true damage scaled off the Grit he took — chip him and you load his gun. Blind does not stop it; it stops Knuckle Down (Q, 9s). - Facebreaker (E, 16s) is the punish window.

edits.before: Track Sett's Haymaker: Shield + true damage. Blind it. When it is down — Vault-blind + R him.
edits.after: Blinding Assault stops Knuckle Down, never Haymaker. The Show Stopper grounds — it denies Vault.

edits.before: Shield + true damage. Blind it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Shield plus true damage off stored Grit — poking him only charges it.

edits.before: Vaulting INTO the fight to feel like an assassin — Vault is your spacing reset, not an engage.
edits.after: The Show Stopper grounds you where it lands — Vault cannot carry you out, so hold Flash for it.

edits.before: Blind (Q) the moment he commits his double-punch passive or grab so his W smash whiffs
edits.after: Blind (Q) his Knuckle Down punches — his empowered autos whiff, though Haymaker still lands

notes: dosFull[2].t reads 'Blind (E) his W-punch' — the blind is Blinding Assault (Q), not Vault (E), and it cannot stop Haymaker at all. It is 21 characters so the applier skips it; it needs a manual fix. Packet games (367) disagrees with the brief's top-level games (534) for this matchup. Packet defect 'never names any of Sett's abilities' is now partly answered on the full layer; the content layer still names none, but its prose is accurate and within band, so I did not burn edits renaming things the reader already understands.
